title: Al-Hakim, the All-Wise
tomorrow: why does 'the Loving' sit right beside 'the Forgiving'?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Wasi', the Vast, wide in mercy and in knowledge, and the line: vast. Last week's six Names fit inside it. A new week opens on a boat.

A group project where the smartest person makes a move nobody understands, and says: trust me, I'll explain later. Now put that on a river. In Surah Al-Kahf, the prophet Musa asks to travel with a servant of God, a man given knowledge from God's own presence; the hadith call him Khidr. Khidr agrees on one condition: ask me nothing until I explain. They're taken aboard a boat by its owners, poor men who work the water, and Khidr calmly knocks a hole in its side.
screen: `TRUST ME, I'LL EXPLAIN LATER.` → `MUSA AND KHIDR.` → `A HOLE IN THE BOAT.`

segments.voice: Musa can't hold it in: you've holed their boat! Khidr reminds him of the deal. Two more scenes follow, each harder to watch, until Musa breaks the deal a third time, and Khidr explains everything. The boat? A king up the river was seizing every sound boat by force. A damaged one would be left for its poor owners. The broken wall Khidr rebuilt for free, in a town that refused them food? A treasure for two orphan boys lay beneath it, kept safe until they grew up. What looked like damage was protection. That's today's Name: Al-Hakim, the All-Wise, whose wisdom puts each thing in its place, even when the place makes no sense from where you stand. When the angels in Surah Al-Baqarah admit what they don't know, they say: "Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise." And notice what the Qur'an keeps in. Musa objects every time, out loud, and the story doesn't cut it. Trusting a wisdom you can't see isn't pretending nothing's wrong. It's staying on the boat while you ask. Here's the detail to tell a friend tonight. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says he wished Musa had been patient a little longer, so that more of their story would have been told.
screen: `MUSA PROTESTS.` · `THE KING, THE WALL, THE TREASURE.` · `AL-HAKIM: EACH THING IN ITS PLACE.` · `STAY ON THE BOAT WHILE YOU ASK.` · then, large: `WISE.`

segments.voice: Look at one thing near you that you didn't understand at first: a scar, a hand-me-down, a book someone pushed on you, a gift that seemed odd. Rest your eyes on it, or on its memory, for a few slow breaths. Then let the sit hold a quiet question: what else might not be in its place yet, from where I stand?
screen: `ONE THING YOU DIDN'T UNDERSTAND AT FIRST.` · `REST YOUR EYES ON IT.` · `WHAT ELSE CAN'T I SEE YET?`

segments.voice: Al-Hakim. The All-Wise, who puts each thing in its place, boats and walls included. Name forty-six.
Keep this: wise, because a hole in a boat can be a rescue. That's day ninety-four.

chat.meaning: Khidr's damage turned out to be protection, and Musa still spoke up. Trusting Al-Hakim doesn't mean not asking; it means not deciding the meaning too soon.
